input.question: How quickly does a small service business need to return a missed call to keep the lead?

sources.text: Missed-call study, 2025, 1,200 small service firms. 62 percent of callers who reached voicemail did not call again. Firms that called back within one hour booked the job in 48 percent of cases; after 24 hours the figure fell to 11 percent. The authors note the sample is mostly trades and clinics.
sources.title: Missed calls in small service firms

sources.text: SME customer survey, 2026, 800 respondents. Firms that returned calls the same day kept three in four enquiries. The survey found no meaningful difference between a callback in one hour and a callback later the same day. Respondents were recruited online and self-reported.
sources.title: SME customer survey 2026

sources.text: Casey's notes from three assessments this autumn: front desks returned voicemails two or three days late in two of the three firms. Nobody tracked how many of those callers had already booked elsewhere.

input.question: What do the two scheduling tools charge, and how do they differ on text reminders and setup fees?

sources.text: Vendor A scheduling software: 29 dollars per user per month, billed annually. Includes text reminders up to 500 messages a month; further messages cost extra. No setup fee.
sources.title: Vendor A pricing page

sources.text: Vendor B scheduling software: flat 149 dollars per month for up to ten users. Text reminders are unlimited. A one-time setup fee of 300 dollars applies.
sources.title: Vendor B pricing page

input.question: Do text reminders reduce no-shows for dental hygiene recalls?

sources.text: Interview with a dental practice owner. 'We tried text reminders for hygiene recalls in the spring. No-shows went from roughly one in eight to one in fifteen over three months. Postcards never moved the number.' She added that two older patients complained about texts.
Trade article on patient recalls. The author says text reminders are 'widely believed' to cut no-shows but cites no data. It recommends keeping a phone call for patients over seventy.
sources.title: Recalls that work

input.question: How widely are small firms using AI tools, and for what?

sources.text: 2026 small-business AI report, 2,000 firms under fifty staff. 41 percent use at least one AI tool weekly. The most common use is drafting emails and documents. Only 9 percent have changed a core process because of AI.
sources.title: Small-business AI report 2026

sources.text: Poll of 300 accounting firms, 2026. 58 percent use an AI tool weekly, mainly for document summaries. Partners named data privacy as the main reason for not going further.
sources.title: Accounting firms poll
